policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The cube slides back and forth along a line that passes through the target; every time it crosses the target line counts as one arrival at the target. The goal instruction names the ordinal N (second, third, fifth...). The button must be pressed one arrival early: when N-1 arrivals have happened and the cube is on its way back toward the target, so the press lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time. An episode starts in A: at the first step (empty memory, gripper raised out of the frame and not yet above the button) choose A 'move to the top of the button to prepare'. No point is needed. At every later step (gripper is already positioned above the button, fingers closed), first update memory as instructed (crossings, cube_side, first_cross_t; the crossing that brings crossings to N-1 often happens inside the frames of the very step where the decision is made), then decide using the updated crossings and first_cross_t values and the cube motion in this step's frames: - Predict the timing. The cube starts at rest at one extreme of its swing at t=0, so first_cross_t is a quarter period and the Nth arrival at the target is predicted at T_N = (2N-1)*first_cross_t. Compute remaining = T_N - (timestep of the scene at this decision step). While first_cross_t is empty, crossings is 0 and no timing is needed. - Determine the cube's direction from the last two frames shown at this step, using their timesteps: v = (cube_x at the last frame - cube_x at the previous frame) / (last timestep - previous timestep). Always divide by the time gap. Take the cube's side at the last frame (smaller_x if cube_x < target_x, larger_x if cube_x > target_x). The cube is HEADING BACK toward the target if it is on the larger_x side and v < 0, or on the smaller_x side and v > 0, or its cube_x is identical in the last two frames (fully stopped at the turnaround). Otherwise it is RUNNING OUT (moving away from the target on its current side); this includes the case where the two frames lie on different sides, since the cube has just crossed. Do not treat a small |v| as the turnaround: cube speed varies by a factor of three across episodes, and a slow cube that has just crossed is still far from returning. Do not use |cube_x - target_x| shrinking or growing as the test: it shrinks across a crossing even though the cube is then moving away. - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if crossings == N-1 AND any of: (a) remaining <= 35 timesteps (the press takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land); (b) remaining <= first_cross_t + 4 (the cube is at or past its predicted turnaround, which comes a quarter period before T_N); (c) the cube is HEADING BACK by the test above. No point is needed. - Otherwise choose B 'remain static'. This covers: crossings < N-1 (even if the cube is heading toward the target, let it pass), and crossings == N-1 while the cube is RUNNING OUT by the test above with remaining > 35 and remaining > first_cross_t + 4 (including the step right after the (N-1)th crossing, however slowly the cube is gliding, and while it is still on its way out to the far end). If crossings somehow exceeds N-1, or the situation matches no rule above, choose C immediately if the cube is HEADING BACK by the test above or remaining <= 35, otherwise B. Never choose A after the first step.

fields.name: crossings
fields.description: Take the crossings count carried in (0 at the first step, since memory is empty). Build the sequence: the carried-in cube_side (skip if memory is empty), then the side (cube_x < target_x -> smaller_x, cube_x > target_x -> larger_x) of each frame shown at this step in time order, ending with the scene at this step. Add 1 for every consecutive pair in that sequence whose side differs. Write the result. e.g. 2

fields.name: cube_side
fields.description: The side of the target line the cube is on in the last frame shown at this step (the scene at this decision step): 'smaller_x' if cube_x < target_x, 'larger_x' if cube_x > target_x. Overwrite it every step. e.g. larger_x

fields.name: first_cross_t
fields.description: Carry it unchanged if it is already set. If it is empty and the crossings count you just computed at this step is 1 or more, find the first consecutive pair in this step's side sequence whose side differs. If both are frames of this step, write the timestep at which cube_x would equal target_x by linear interpolation between those two frames, rounded to the nearest whole timestep. If the flip is between the carried-in cube_side and this step's first frame, extrapolate backwards linearly from this step's first two frames (cube_x and timestep) to the timestep at which cube_x would equal target_x, and round. Otherwise leave it empty. e.g. 30
